h1: SEO costs in Kolkata and what the low prices hide
metaTitle: What Is the Cost of SEO in Kolkata? Real Bands
metaDescription: Kolkata SEO packages advertise from ₹3,000 a month. Here's the salary maths behind that number, what it can't cover, and what a fair quote looks like.
answer: Kolkata SEO packages advertise from about ₹3,000 a month and run past ₹50,000. At city salary costs, ₹3,000 buys roughly four to six hours of junior time — under an hour a week. A quote worth taking seriously for a competitive keyword set starts closer to ₹25,000–₹40,000 a month.
takeaways: Kolkata has the lowest advertised SEO entry price of any Indian metro. That's a salary story, not a value story.
Do the division before you sign: **retainer ÷ realistic hourly cost = hours a month**. At ₹3,000 the answer is under six.
Local scope is genuinely cheaper here. National scope is not — you'll be competing with Bengaluru and Gurgaon budgets regardless of where your office is.
The staffing questions at the bottom of this page will tell you more in five minutes than any package comparison.

body: Kolkata's advertised SEO market has three visible tiers, and the gap between the bottom and the top is wider here than in almost any other Indian metro.

At the bottom you'll see monthly packages listed from around ₹3,000, with a dense band between ₹5,000 and ₹10,000. In the middle sit boutique agencies and experienced freelancers at ₹15,000–₹40,000. At the top, a small number of firms — usually the ones also serving clients in Bengaluru, Gurgaon or overseas — quote ₹50,000 and up, at which point the price is set by the scope of work rather than by the city.

Treat those numbers as market observation rather than survey data; nobody publishes an audited price index for this. But the shape is consistent, and the bottom tier is the one worth examining, because it's what most Kolkata businesses buy first.

sections.h2: The salary maths behind a ₹3,000 retainer
body: This is arithmetic, not opinion, and it takes about ninety seconds.

An SEO executive in Kolkata earns meaningfully less than the same role in Bengaluru or Gurgaon — the city's overall salary base is lower and always has been. Call it ₹18,000–₹30,000 a month for someone with a year or two of experience. Now load it: employer contributions, a desk, a laptop, a share of the tool licences, supervision from someone senior, and the reality that only about two-thirds of paid hours are ever billable to a client. That takes the real cost to something like ₹30,000–₹50,000 a month for roughly 110–120 productive hours.

That's ₹260–₹450 an hour at cost. Add the margin any business needs to survive — rent, sales, the months a client doesn't pay on time — and a sellable rate lands somewhere around ₹450–₹700 an hour for junior execution work.

Divide ₹3,000 by that and you get four to six hours a month. Not four to six hours of strategy. Four to six hours of everything: research, writing, fixes, reporting, and the email thread you're currently having with them.

callout.title: Under an hour a week
callout.body: ₹3,000 a month at a Kolkata agency's realistic junior rate buys 4–6 hours. That's roughly 45 minutes a week on your account, across every discipline, including the time spent writing the report that tells you what they did with the 45 minutes.

sections.h2: What the cheap tier can contain, and what it physically can't
body: Four to six hours is not nothing. It's just a very specific something, and it's worth knowing which side of the line each promise falls on before you read a deliverable list.

bullets: A monthly tool export flagging the same issues as last month.
One or two short articles, usually written to a keyword rather than to a buyer.
Directory and citation submissions — countable, fast, and mostly worthless in 2026.
A rank-tracking screenshot for keywords chosen because they're winnable, not because anyone buys from them.
Basic Google Business Profile upkeep, which is the one item on this list with real value for a local business.

subs.h3: What cannot fit, at any price this low
bullets: **Technical work with your developer.** A single redirect audit and spec takes longer than the whole monthly allocation.
**Content written by someone who spoke to you.** An interview, a draft, an edit and a publish is 6–10 hours for one page.
**Earned links.** A genuine placement takes hours of research, pitching and follow-up per link. What arrives instead is a network placement, and that's a liability rather than an asset.
**Anyone senior thinking about your business.** Strategy is the first thing removed, because it's the thing you can't see missing for a quarter.

callout.title: The cost that isn't on the invoice
callout.body: Cheap link packages come from sites built to sell links. Google's spam systems recognise those patterns well, and cleaning up a poisoned link profile costs far more than the retainer ever saved. The ₹5,000 package can end up being the most expensive thing you buy that year.

sections.h2: Local scope versus national scope: the question that actually sets your price
body: Almost every argument about Kolkata SEO pricing is really an argument about scope that nobody named out loud.

Local scope is genuinely cheaper, and honestly so. A single-location business here — a diagnostics lab in Salt Lake, a coaching institute in Ballygunge, a boutique in Gariahat, a packers-and-movers operation, a dental clinic — is competing for map-pack positions and city-modified queries against other local businesses. The work is Google Business Profile accuracy, review volume and pace, local citations, service and area pages that read like a human wrote them, and site speed on the mobile connections your customers actually use. That's a real job, and ₹15,000–₹25,000 a month covers it properly for one location.

There's a second local factor worth budgeting for: Bengali-language search. For consumer categories — healthcare, education, food, retail, property — a share of your audience searches in Bengali or in transliterated Bengali, and almost nobody in the city is writing for it well. It costs more per page and it faces far less competition, which is an unusually good trade.

National scope is a different purchase entirely. If you're an exporter, a B2B manufacturer, a SaaS product or a D2C brand shipping across India, you are competing in the same results as companies funding ₹1,50,000-a-month programmes. Buying a ₹10,000 Kolkata package for that job isn't thrift; it's a category error. The honest options are to narrow the target set until it's winnable at your budget, or to raise the budget. [What SEO costs across India](/answers/how-much-does-seo-cost-in-india) sets out the bands, and [what an SEO agency in Kolkata should look like](/seo-agency/kolkata) covers the local market in more detail.

sections.h2: Six staffing questions to ask a Kolkata agency
body: Skip the package comparison. These six questions expose more in five minutes, and every one of them has a right answer that a competent agency gives without hesitating.
numbered: **"How many hours a month does my retainer buy, and split by whose hours?"** A planned engagement answers in ten seconds. "We don't track hours, we focus on outcomes" is a fine answer only if the contract contains an outcome.
**"How many live accounts does the person working on my site handle?"** Above five or six, your month is being rationed. Ask for the number, not the reassurance.

**"Which tools do you pay for, and can I see a live login during the call?"** Ahrefs, Semrush and a proper crawler cost real money annually. A shop selling ₹5,000 packages cannot afford them per client, and shared or cracked access is common at that price.
**"Where exactly do your links come from — show me three you built last quarter."** "Our network" means a private blog network. Real answers come with URLs you can open.
**"Who writes the content, and will they interview someone on my team?"** If nobody talks to your experts, you're buying rewritten competitor copy, and so is everyone else in your category.

**"What number are we measuring, what is it today, and what happens if it doesn't move?"** The last clause is the one that separates the field. Nobody honest promises a ranking position — Google's index isn't theirs to promise. A commitment against your own baseline is a real commitment.

faqs.q: What is the cost of SEO in Kolkata per month?
faqs.a: Advertised packages start near ₹3,000 and the visible market thins out around ₹50,000. Realistically, ₹15,000–₹25,000 a month covers a single-location local business properly, and ₹25,000–₹50,000 is the band where a competitive keyword set becomes possible. Below ₹10,000 you're buying under two hours a week.

faqs.q: Why is SEO cheaper in Kolkata than in Bengaluru or Mumbai?
faqs.a: Salaries. Kolkata has the lowest cost base of the major Indian metros, so an agency's loaded cost per productive hour is lower and it can quote less for the same hours. What doesn't change is the difficulty of the ranking itself — if you compete nationally, your rivals are funding Bengaluru rates to outrank you.

faqs.q: Are ₹3,000 SEO packages in Kolkata a scam?
faqs.a: Not necessarily a scam — usually a different product. At city rates, ₹3,000 buys four to six hours a month, which covers a recycled audit, a short article and some directory submissions. It becomes genuinely harmful when it includes network link placements, because cleaning those up costs more than the package ever saved.

faqs.q: How much should a small Kolkata business spend on SEO?
faqs.a: For one location competing on local and map-pack queries, ₹15,000–₹25,000 a month is enough to do the work properly: Google Business Profile, reviews, citations, service and area pages, and site speed. Spend less and you're paying for activity; spend more only when you start targeting queries beyond the city.

faqs.q: Does Bengali-language SEO cost more in Kolkata?
faqs.a: Per page, yes — you need writers who are genuinely fluent, not translation tools. But competition for Bengali and transliterated queries is far thinner than for the English equivalents, so the cost per acquired position is often lower. It's most worthwhile for consumer categories like healthcare, education, food and property.
